newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 31.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Jan. 31
WASHINGTON - The D.C. government is failing to collect tens of millions of dollars in taxes and its financial operations are in such chaos that officials can't rely on their own budget numbers.

WASHINGTON - The Federal Election Commission, in a plea for more funding, told Congress it has failed to move swiftly against politicians who violate campaign finance laws and said there were abuses from the 1996 campaign that deserved immediate investigation.

WASHINGTON - The White House became enmeshed in a new controversy over whether it improperly mixed official and political business after disclosures that aides to President Clinton shared information from a government database with the Democratic National Committee.
NEW YORK - Former heavyweight boxing champion Riddick Bowe announced a rather radical training program -- he has joined the U.S. Marine Corps Reserve.

WASHINGTON - FBI specialists investigating the Oklahoma City bombing reached early conclusions based on little or no scientific analysis, failed to take precautions to avoid contamination of some evidence and engaged in shoddy lab work, according to allegations developed in a Justice Department investigation.
WASHINGTON - The Saudi Arabian military is preparing a request to buy 102 F-16 jet fighters from the United States worth $5 billion to $15 billion, industry and diplomatic officials said.
